# ASR Configurator
> Interactive configuration tool for Microsoft Defender Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules.
> URL: https://asrconfigurator.pages.dev
> Full Technical Bundle: https://asrconfigurator.pages.dev/llms-full.txt
> GitHub: https://github.com/Ashutoshgit47/ASR-Configurator
> Author: Ashutosh Gautam

## Overview
ASR Configurator is a client-side web application designed to help system administrators and security engineers configure, customize, and deploy Microsoft Defender Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules with confidence.

Features:
- Full coverage of all 19 Microsoft Defender ASR rules.
- 5 curated security posture presets: Disabled, Basic Protection, Balanced (Recommended), Strict Protection, and Developer-Friendly.
- Instant code generation for PowerShell (`Set-MpPreference`), Group Policy (`.reg` / GPO), and Microsoft Intune (Settings Catalog JSON & OMA-URI).
- Single-click copy, bulk actions, rule search, and category filtering.
- Client-side only: no telemetry, no tracking, no server calls.

## Rule Action Values
Microsoft Defender ASR rules use the following numeric values:
- `0`: Disabled (Rule is inactive; no blocking or logging)
- `1`: Block (Matching behavior is actively stopped; logs Event ID 1121)
- `2`: Audit (Behavior is permitted but logged under Event ID 1122 for evaluation)
- `6`: Warn (Prompts user with a warning before allowing; supported by select rules)

## Complete Microsoft Defender ASR Rules Reference (19 Rules)

1. Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers
   - GUID: 56A863A9-875E-4185-98A7-B882C64B5CE5
   - Category: System | Risk: LOW
   - Description: Prevents malicious drivers from loading even if signed.

2. Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes
   - GUID: 7674BA52-37EB-4A4F-A9A1-F0F9A1619A2C
   - Category: App | Risk: MEDIUM
   - Description: Stops Adobe Reader from spawning other programs (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe).

3. Block all Office applications from creating child processes
   - GUID: D4F940AB-401B-4EFC-AADC-AD5F3C50688A
   - Category: Office | Risk: HIGH
   - Description: Prevents Word, Excel, and PowerPoint from launching child processes.

4. Block credential stealing from LSASS
   - GUID: 9E6C4E1F-7D60-472F-BA1A-A39EF669E4B2
   - Category: Credential | Risk: LOW
   - Description: Protects Windows Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) from memory dumping tools (e.g. Mimikatz).

5. Block executable content from email client and webmail
   - GUID: BE9BA2D9-53EA-4CDC-84E5-9B1EEEE46550
   - Category: Email | Risk: LOW
   - Description: Prevents running executables and scripts directly from email clients and webmail.

6. Block executable files unless they meet prevalence, age, or trusted list
   - GUID: 01443614-CD74-433A-B99E-2ECDC07BFC25
   - Category: App | Risk: CRITICAL
   - Description: Only allows execution of reputable files backed by Microsoft Cloud-delivered protection.

7. Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts
   - GUID: 5BEB7EFE-FD9A-4556-801D-275E5FFC04CC
   - Category: Script | Risk: MEDIUM
   - Description: Detects and blocks scripts using obfuscation or evasion techniques.

8. Block JavaScript/VBScript from launching downloaded executables
   - GUID: D3E037E1-3EB8-44C8-A917-57927947596D
   - Category: Web | Risk: LOW
   - Description: Prevents scripts from downloading and launching secondary executables.

9. Block Office applications from creating executable content
   - GUID: 3B576869-A4EC-4529-8536-B80A7769E899
   - Category: Office | Risk: MEDIUM
   - Description: Stops Office applications from writing .exe, .dll, or script payloads to disk.

10. Block Office apps from injecting code into other processes
    - GUID: 75668C1F-73B5-4CF0-BB93-3ECF5CB7CC84
    - Category: Office | Risk: MEDIUM
    - Description: Blocks code injection attempts from Office apps into other running processes.

11. Block Office communication apps from creating child processes
    - GUID: 26190899-1602-49E8-8B27-EB1D0A1CE869
    - Category: Email | Risk: MEDIUM
    - Description: Prevents Microsoft Outlook from launching child processes.

12. Block persistence through WMI event subscription
    - GUID: E6DB77E5-3DF2-4CF1-B95A-636979351E5B
    - Category: System | Risk: LOW
    - Description: Prevents malware from abusing Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) event subscriptions for persistence.

13. Block process creations from PSExec and WMI commands
    - GUID: D1E49AAC-8F56-4280-B9BA-993A6D77406C
    - Category: Remote | Risk: MEDIUM
    - Description: Blocks remote process creation originating from PsExec and WMI commands.

14. Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB
    - GUID: B2B3F03D-6A65-4F7B-A9C7-1C7EF74A9BA4
    - Category: USB | Risk: LOW
    - Description: Prevents unsigned executable processes from running off removable USB media.

15. Block Win32 API calls from Office macros
    - GUID: 92E97FA1-2EDF-4476-BDD6-9DD0B4DDDC7B
    - Category: Office | Risk: HIGH
    - Description: Prevents VBA macros inside Office documents from calling Win32 APIs directly.

16. Use advanced protection against ransomware
    - GUID: C1DB55AB-C21A-4637-BB3F-A12568109D35
    - Category: Ransomware | Risk: LOW
    - Description: Uses heuristics and cloud analysis to detect and block ransomware encryption behaviors.

17. Block rebooting machine in Safe Mode
    - GUID: 33DDEDF1-C6E0-47CB-833E-DE6133960387
    - Category: System | Risk: LOW
    - Description: Prevents attackers from using bcdedit/bootcfg to force a machine into Safe Mode to bypass security agents.

18. Block Webshell creation for Servers
    - GUID: A8F5898E-1DC8-49A9-9878-85004B8A61E6
    - Category: Server | Risk: HIGH
    - Description: Blocks web shell script creation on Windows Server running Microsoft Exchange.

19. Block use of copied or impersonated system tools
    - GUID: C0033C00-D16D-4114-A5A0-DC9B3A7D2CEB
    - Category: System | Risk: MEDIUM
    - Description: Blocks executable files copied from system directories (%windir%\System32 or SysWOW64) or impersonating system tools from running in other locations.

## Deployment Syntax Examples

### PowerShell
```powershell
Set-MpPreference -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids @("9E6C4E1F-7D60-472F-BA1A-A39EF669E4B2", "D4F940AB-401B-4EFC-AADC-AD5F3C50688A") -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Actions @(1, 2)
```

### Intune OMA-URI
- Path: `./Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/Defender/AttackSurfaceReductionRules`
- Type: String
- Value format: `<GUID>=<Action>` (newline-separated)

### Group Policy Registry Location
```reg
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR]
"ExploitGuard_ASR_Rules"=dword:00000001

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules]
"9E6C4E1F-7D60-472F-BA1A-A39EF669E4B2"="1"
"D4F940AB-401B-4EFC-AADC-AD5F3C50688A"="2"
```

## Recommended Deployment Lifecycle
1. Audit Mode (2): Enable all desired rules in Audit mode for 30–60 days to monitor logs (Event ID 1122).
2. Triage & Exclusions: Identify legitimate business applications that triggered events and create path/hash exclusions.
3. Block Mode (1): Gradually transition tested rules to Block mode (Event ID 1121).
